description: Regueiro-Picallo, Manuel at Universidade da Coruña publishes annular-flume measurements testing temperature-based sewer-sediment estimation through Co-UDlabs. A controlled-temperature system reproduces sewer patterns while changing flow, sediment depth and temperature conditions. The campaign tests the influence of hydrodynamics on inferred accumulation, distinct from the baseline heat-transfer and gully-pot campaigns. Coverage is the University of Sheffield ANNULAR flume; exact campaign dates and sample frequency are unspecified. Zenodo provides a data ZIP and a PDF storage report with free access under CC BY-NC 4.0. These observations support the source-defined drainage measurement, physical-model or simulation activity. Related Co-UDlabs experiments describe other assets and test conditions; they are not assumed to be independent or interchangeable measurements. A limitation is steady laboratory flow and temperature control differ from field sewers, and a record of experimental conditions does not guarantee accurate sediment estimates elsewhere. Only native metadata and file descriptors were read; no data values, archive, code or report body was obtained.
